features.name: academic credential
features.description: Captures the formal level of technical education the applicant presents as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience only, with no advanced degree presented.
Master's degree in computer science or a related field is presented.
Doctoral degree in computer science or a related field is presented.

features.evidence: 7 years at Amazon testing, maintaining, and launching production services
features.name: professional tenure
features.description: Captures the amount of post-school software engineering experience the letter claims.

levels.descriptor: Roughly entry-to-early career tenure, around 2 to 3 years, or unclear total experience.
Solid mid-level tenure, around 4 to 5 years.
Seasoned tenure, around 6 or more years.

features.name: delivery volume
features.description: Captures how many distinct production services the applicant says they have tested, maintained, or launched.

levels.descriptor: Only 1 to 2 production services are cited, or shipped-system breadth is unclear.
About 3 to 4 production services are cited.
5 or more production services are cited, signaling broader delivery exposure.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents Python as a central production language for services, tooling, or automation.

levels.descriptor: No Python evidence, or only a passing mention that does not show real working fluency.
Python experience is stated, but depth or scope is only lightly described.
Python is framed as extensive or daily production work across services, automation, analysis, or internal tooling.

features.name: security assessment practice
features.description: Captures direct experience reviewing systems for security issues through threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, or validation of fixes.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment experience is stated.
Security assessment experience is asserted in general terms, but methods or contexts are thin.
Structured hands-on assessment work is described with concrete practices such as threat modeling, reviewing unfamiliar code, or validating remediations.

features.evidence: automates triage of incoming vulnerability reports
features.name: vulnerability workflow automation
features.description: Captures experience building software that classifies, deduplicates, routes, or otherwise automates vulnerability intake and triage.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-handling automation is described.
Automation of vulnerability work is mentioned, but the workflow or contribution is vague.
Clear ownership of a vulnerability triage pipeline is described, with specific functions such as classification, deduplication, routing, or queue reduction.

features.evidence: Python agents supervised by Go services
features.name: agentic systems design
features.description: Captures experience designing agent-based tooling rather than only ordinary backend systems or generic AI features.

levels.descriptor: No agentic system experience is stated.
Agent systems are mentioned at a high level, but architecture and control model remain vague.
A concrete agent architecture is described, including Python agents plus Go-based guardrails, supervision, auditing, or bounded actions.

features.evidence: shipping LLM-backed features and hardening them against unpredictable inputs
features.name: applied AI production work
features.description: Captures direct experience deploying AI or LLM functionality in production and reasoning about its reliability.

levels.descriptor: No AI or LLM experience is stated.
AI or LLM production use is mentioned, but without operational detail.
AI work is described with evaluation, hardening, trust, or explicit handling of failure modes in production.

features.evidence: redesigning an in-memory index that sat on our hottest request path
features.name: algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows practical mastery of data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering examples.

levels.descriptor: No evidence of data-structure or algorithmic strength is given.
A general claim of DS&A strength is made and anchored by at least one example.
A specific redesign or optimization story shows DS&A materially improved a real system.

features.name: security credential strength
features.description: Captures the rigor of formal security certification presented in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A baseline credential such as Security+ is presented.
A hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP is presented.

features.name: offensive practice
features.description: Captures how much the applicant demonstrates an active attacker-oriented practice outside ordinary product engineering.

levels.descriptor: No offensive practice is mentioned.
CTF participation or similar attacker practice is mentioned, but without strong evidence of depth.
Serious offensive practice is shown through strong CTF results, sustained competition, or clearly advanced attacker-oriented work.

features.evidence: maintain an open-source project with a real community
features.name: open-source ownership
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows public engineering contribution beyond private employer work.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional patches, upstream fixes, or limited contributions.
The applicant presents ongoing stewardship such as maintaining a project, reviewing contributions, cutting releases, or owning a library used by others.

features.evidence: built a distributed rate-limiting service with coordinated state across nodes
features.name: personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical scope and seriousness of self-directed engineering work described outside the day job.

levels.descriptor: No side project is mentioned, or only a very small personal utility appears.
A modest standalone application or tool is described, but without substantial systems complexity.
A substantial self-directed systems project is described, especially one involving storage, distribution, replication, or failure recovery.

features.evidence: benefits accrue broadly across an organization
features.name: platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures whether the applicant explicitly values central infrastructure work whose impact compounds across many teams.

levels.descriptor: No platform-level or organization-wide leverage framing is present.
The letter expresses generic interest in scale or broad impact.
The letter explicitly frames motivation around foundational infrastructure, inherited improvements, or organization-wide leverage.

features.evidence: helping busy developer teams do the secure thing by default
features.name: developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security engineering as making other engineers safer and more effective rather than merely auditing them.

levels.descriptor: No developer-enablement framing is present.
There is a general service orientation, but the applicant does not clearly articulate how security should help developers.
The letter explicitly emphasizes secure-by-default tooling, assisting developer teams, or avoiding a policing posture.

features.evidence: too many signals, too few experts
features.name: role-specific mission insight
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter identifies the actual problem this team solves, such as scaling scarce security expertise through automation, triage, agents, or variant analysis.

levels.descriptor: Motivation stays generic, such as liking Google, backend work, or security in broad terms.
The letter mentions automation or scale, but only in broad, common language.
The letter names the concrete bottleneck or workflow in this role, showing real understanding of security automation at organizational scale.

features.evidence: deduplicating findings and routing them to the owning teams
features.name: achievement concreteness
features.description: Captures how often claims are backed by concrete mechanisms, examples, or outcomes rather than by unsupported adjectives.

levels.descriptor: Most claims are generic assertions of skill or fit, with little evidence of what was actually built.
Some claims are anchored in examples, but many remain broad or unsubstantiated.
The letter repeatedly gives specific technical actions, mechanisms, or outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to picture.

features.name: proofreading accuracy
features.description: Captures how much spelling and typographical noise distracts from or undermines the application.

levels.descriptor: Frequent or disruptive spelling and typographical errors appear throughout the letter.
There are noticeable errors, but they are limited enough that the letter remains easy to read.
The writing is clean or nearly clean, with little proofreading noise.
